shared_context.content: For an integer m >= 0 and a sign sequence u of length m-1 when m >= 1 (and u = empty when m = 0), U_m(u) denotes the number of permutations (b_1,...,b_m) of {1,...,m} such that u_i * (b_{i+1} - b_i) > 0 for every 1 <= i <= m-1. By convention U_0(empty) = 1.
shared_context.label: U_m(u)

shared_context.content: For m >= 1 and u = (u_1,...,u_{m-1}), define Peak(u) subseteq {1,...,m} by: if m = 1 then Peak(u) = {1}; if m >= 2 then 1 is in Peak(u) iff u_1 = -1, m is in Peak(u) iff u_{m-1} = +1, and for 2 <= j <= m-1 one has j in Peak(u) iff u_{j-1} = +1 and u_j = -1.
shared_context.label: Peak(u)

shared_context.content: For 1 <= j <= m and u = (u_1,...,u_{m-1}), write u^{<j} = (u_1,...,u_{j-2}) and u^{>j} = (u_{j+1},...,u_{m-1}), interpreting these as the empty sequence when the lower index exceeds the upper.
shared_context.label: u^{<j} and u^{>j}

shared_context.content: For m >= 1, alt_m^+ is the sign sequence of length m-1 with i-th entry (-1)^(i-1), i.e. (+1,-1,+1,-1,...), and alt_m^- is the sign sequence of length m-1 with i-th entry (-1)^i, i.e. (-1,+1,-1,+1,...). For m in {0,1} these are empty. Define E_m := U_m(alt_m^+), so E_0 = 1.
shared_context.label: Alternating patterns and E_m

shared_context.content: For the theorem's fixed n and sign sequence s of length n-1, the quantity f(s) in the statement is exactly U_n(s).
shared_context.label: Relation with the theorem's f(s)

strategy_summary: Prove the theorem by strong induction on n using the position of the largest value n. For a sign pattern s, the possible positions of n form a nonadjacent peak set Peak(s), and counting by the position of n gives a binomial convolution over smaller sign patterns. Replacing each smaller count by the alternating upper bound E_m reduces the problem to a weighted independent-set problem on the path {1,...,n}. A bottleneck lemma shows that for the resulting Euler-type weights, the maximum independent-set weight is attained exactly by the full odd or full even parity class; those parity classes correspond exactly to the two alternating sign sequences.
